question: 52 oranges are bought for ₹ 119.60 and sold at the rate of ₹ 41.40 per dozen. The profit percentage is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) of 1 dozen oranges = (119.60 ÷ 52) × 12 = ₹ 27.60

Selling Price (SP) of 1 dozen oranges = ₹ 41.40

Profit = SP − CP = 41.40 − 27.60 = ₹ 13.80

Profit % = (13.80 ÷ 27.60) × 100 = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

CP of 52 oranges = ₹ 119.60

SP of 1 dozen (12 oranges) = ₹ 41.40

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 CP = ₹ 27.60

 
 Profit = ₹ 13.80
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 SP = ₹ 41.40 (Per Dozen)

 

 

 +50% Profit

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of 1 orange = 119.60 ÷ 52 = ₹ 2.30

⇒ SP of 1 orange = 41.40 ÷ 12 = ₹ 3.45

⇒ Profit on 1 orange = 3.45 − 2.30 = ₹ 1.15

⇒ Profit % = (1.15 ÷ 2.30) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 2) × 100 = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Formula: Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discounts

When two discounts d₁% and d₂% are applied successively, Effective Discount = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer claims to sell at CP but uses a false weight, Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.
